howToRegenerate: node scripts/check-content.mjs --print-baseline  (prints this shape; it never writes it)
ruleOfExit: A pair leaves this file when the copy is deleted or a ruling settles it. It is NOT kept with status 'resolved': a signature in this file is an exemption, so keeping a closed pair would let the same duplicate ship again without going red. The three pairs closed by S018/D262 are listed in `resolved` below for provenance only.

resolved.pair: band's Meetup/chat twin <> hero's date-and-chat line
resolved.how: the band's line deleted; the hero keeps the one statement of where dates and discussion live

resolved.pair: hero syllabus line <> band's homework line
resolved.how: the band's homework line deleted; the hero's syllabus sentence now carries the chat statement too

resolved.pair: hero threads signpost <> 'What we take up' opener
resolved.how: the hero signpost became the syllabus line; the section opener kept its sourcing clause, because check:content refuses an unsourced list (D92)

scores: content words only; sentences split on terminal punctuation only. A pair is a pair when it shares >=3 content words and (Jaccard >= 0.45 or overlap >= 0.5). Overlap is shared words over the SHORTER sentence, because a paraphrase of a long sentence scores low on Jaccard alone.

statusMeaning.open: the repeat is real and unruled: the gate stays green on it; deleting one side or taking a ruling is the exit
statusMeaning.deliberate: the repeat is the point of the surface - a source line or a ruling says so, in why
statusMeaning.template: identical row furniture on sibling rows: one string rendered twice. Coupling, not duplication - if one row changes, both must

pairs.signature: copied from the club's own calendar on nov 6 2026 <> the signup is on meetup and the date above is copied from the club's own calendar
pairs.surfaces: section:When We Meet (homepage compact band) <> section:Parallel Learning for Mathematical Minds (event row)
pairs.why: Both surfaces draw a date from the same snapshot and each states its provenance where the date is painted - the same rule records 0010/0011 exist for. Accepted: the repeat is the source line, not decorative copy. It becomes a defect only if one of the two stops carrying a date or a source.

pairs.signature: copied from the club's own calendar on nov 6 2026 <> these dates are copied from the club's own calendar
pairs.surfaces: section:When We Meet (/schedule) <> section:MPLS Math Club Social (/schedule event row)
pairs.why: The same provenance rule on the schedule page: the page lede and each row that prints a date say where the date came from.

pairs.signature: details and signup on meetup opens in a new tab <> details and signup on meetup opens in a new tab
pairs.surfaces: section:Parallel Learning for Mathematical Minds <> section:MPLS Math Club Social
pairs.why: Not two sentences - one row template rendered for two events. The gate cannot tell row furniture from copy, so the pair is recorded rather than exempted by a special case. If a future round rewords one row, this row goes stale and the pair goes red: that is the coupling enforced, not a false positive.
